summary: This document details the training of a Deep Q-Network agent to play Ms. Pac-Man, achieving a mean score increase from 492 to 1,342 over five evaluation games. The successful training was attributed primarily to increasing the replay buffer capacity from 5,000 to 2,500,000 and implementing a performance fix for the ring buffer sampling.
key_facts: The agent was trained using a Deep Q-Network over 5,000 episodes.
Mean score improved from 492 to 1,342 across five evaluation games.
The replay buffer capacity was increased from 5,000 to 2,500,000 transitions.
The training run took 127.7 minutes and involved 3,557,262 agent decisions.
The learning rate remained constant at 1e-4 and exploration at 0.20.
A performance fix replaced the `deque` scan with a list-backed ring buffer for O(1) indexing.
The improvement was statistically significant, achieving t(4) = 7.21 against the untrained baseline.

concepts.name: Deep Q-Network
concepts.definition: A neural network used to approximate the optimal action-value function.
concepts.in_this_source: The agent uses a DQN architecture with 3 convolutional layers and 2 dense layers.

concepts.name: Reinforcement Learning
concepts.definition: A machine learning approach where an agent learns through interaction with an environment.
concepts.in_this_source: The training process involves the agent learning from raw screen pixels to maximize rewards.

concepts.name: Experience Replay
concepts.definition: A technique where past experiences are stored and randomly sampled to break correlations.
concepts.in_this_source: The agent stores experiences in a replay buffer and samples batches of 32 for updates.
